name: KKL Rulebook Takeoff System (merged design: calculation-first spine, evidence layer, real-sheet measurer, claims reconciliation)
summary: KKL's QS hours go into the arithmetic, bookkeeping and monthly reconciliation around drawn lines more than into drawing them, so the system starts as a versioned rules engine (engine.js, ported from the existing calc_trench.py) that turns a small set of primitives a QS types or traces once into every derived BQ line under a per-contract rulebook whose parameters carry a page citation and a named confirmer. That spine gives first minutes back at month 3 (derived TRENCH, CHAMBER, RC-SECTION, PAVEMENT and KERB lines drafted for QS review), a BQ binder that pre-fills the quantity sheet, and by month 6 a claims roll-up that drafts monthly SOPA packs and back-to-back subcon certificates from DR Capture rows with two independent sources per line. Only after that, and only if month-3, month-6 and month-12 stop-loss reviews pass, is a real-sheet measurer (viewports, per-viewport scale, pen-weight classification, path-id provenance) built once in Python as a nightly shadow job with an honest 15.5 person-week budget, its proposals reviewed by QSs in their own PDF tool or the capture app, and each item class graduated per drawing source on KKL's own accuracy ledger. Total build 41.5 person-weeks over 24 months (20.5 year 1, 21.0 year 2), which is exactly a 0.4 FTE builder; run cost about US$250 a month; no server, no drawing pixels to any cloud model, confidential sheets never on GitHub. Expected QS effort: 93% of today at month 6, 82% at month 12, 65% at month 24 (55-60% upside if the claims roll-up and auto-lengths both graduate), measured by a start/pause timer and alternating-sheet A/B, never self-report. A named QS signs every bid, claim and certificate throughout; the engine never signs.
principles: Calculation first: measure or type four primitives (count, length, area, levels) once; every derived line is versioned, golden-tested code over a per-contract rulebook, never a model's number.
No model-emitted number ever becomes a quantity: the Claude API reads text (preambles, BQ lines, schedules, legend wording); geometry code measures; the QS confirms.

Build once, in house style: single-file GitHub Pages apps, CSV/JSON on SharePoint, one office PC for nightly Python jobs; no server, no dual Python/JS implementations, no ML classifier until rule-based classification plateaus.

Evidence before promises: zero-behaviour-change capture where QSs already annotate, a real-sheet regression corpus kept off GitHub, and per class x source gates on KKL's own ledger decide every stage change.

Two kinds of gate: deterministic derived families graduate on rulebook confirmation + golden tests + 300 root-caused clean lines; measured primitives graduate on the digest's statistical gates (200/500 items, median <=1%, p95 <=5%, counts >=98%, zero confident-wrong).

Money-bearing safety is structural: unconfirmed rulebook parameter blocks output, entry cross-checks catch garbage-in, dimension grader blocks export beyond 5%, top-80%-of-value items always human, any money-bearing error in an auto stream rolls the class back.

Provenance on every quantity: engine version, rulebook version, primitive hash or path ids, viewport and scale source, checks passed, QS initials, so any figure can be rebuilt for an SO, MC, subcontractor or adjudicator.

Confidentiality by default: Tier A (nothing leaves KKL) for every LTA/HDB/PUB/MC document unless the contracts person clears it in the register; a code gateway enforces the tier and logs every egress.

Claims are reconciliation, not measurement: DR Capture rows joined through the item library, two sources per line, paid_on and measure_rule per BQ item, SO-certified quantity fed back as truth; never auto-submitted.

Effort is proven by logged minutes per sheet per class with start/pause timers and alternating-sheet A/B; time saved is banked as tender capacity in year one; reviewers are scored on catch rate, not throughput.

architecture.data_flow: Tender: GeBIZ ZIP -> Price Schedule PDF -> BQ binder (Extract, text pages, Tier B/C only) -> bq.json + bq_map; preamble pages -> Preamble-to-Rules preset -> rulebook draft -> QS confirms each money-bearing parameter against its cited page -> rulebook v1 (Tier A: typed from template). Drawings stay on the QS PC: QS types or traces primitives in takeoff/index.html with per-viewport scale confirmed and graded (or the nightly harvester imports Bluebeam markups; or ezdxf reads DXF) -> primitives.json -> engine.js (primitives x rulebook x item library) -> .xlsx quantity sheet with engine vs QS columns and cost readout -> QS reconciles, stamps 'checked by', signs -> CSV, primitives.json, ledger rows to SharePoint. Claims (monthly): DR Capture/DR Verify CSVs + tickets/DOs/weighbridge (Extract on KKL's own Tier C documents) + surface volumes where a project has them -> claims.html joins to bq.json via item library with chainage union and two-source checks -> claim pack, subcon certificate, audit appendix (.xlsx) -> named QS signs -> SharePoint; SO-certified quantities entered back into the ledger. VOs: revision-B primitives -> engine diff -> omissions/additions with pricing basis. Auto-primitives (year 2): nightly job imports every measured sheet into sheet.json, resolves viewports and scale, classifies and measures, scores against QS truth (QS final after chief-QS adjudication plus the workbook figure) with reason codes, and in Stage 2 writes proposals as a KKL-ENGINE annotation layer on a PDF copy that the QS reviews in Bluebeam or the capture app; the nightly diff between proposals and final annotations is the corrections log and regression corpus. Ledger and dashboard recompute per class x source gates, calibration and rollback triggers weekly; the gateway logs every egress.
architecture.confidentiality_tiers: Tier A (default for every LTA, HDB, PUB, JTC and MC-issued document, all NDA/OSA/IPA work): nothing leaves KKL; geometry, OCR and measurement in the browser or on the office PC; rulebook and bq_map typed from client templates; sessions carry no API key. Tier B (cleared per project by the contracts person in the register after reading the NDA): preamble, BQ and schedule text pages may go to the Claude API; no drawing pixels ever. Tier C (KKL's own documents such as tickets, DOs, weighbridge receipts and BQ workbooks, and public sheets such as LTA SDRE): text and images permitted; the civils.ai benchmark trial runs on Tier C sheets only. Enforced by the gateway in code with a per-project egress log; regression corpus of real sheets lives on SharePoint, GitHub Actions sees synthetic sheets only; the contracts person writes down the OSA and NDA reading before Stage 1 and notifies the PI/CAR insurer of AI-assisted quantities with named sign-off.
architecture.repo_layout: GitHub (public house style, no client content): takeoff/index.html (capture app), takeoff/claims.html, takeoff/ledger.html, takeoff/engine.js, takeoff/library/items.json, takeoff/templates/<client>/ (rulebook templates, SDRE lookups, mesh kg/m2 by standard), takeoff/schema/ (sgm, primitives, rulebook, ledger, bq_map), takeoff/tests/*.golden.json and synthetic round trips, takeoff/jobs/ (harvest.py, import_pdf.py, import_dxf.py, scale.py, classify.py, kernel.py, shadow.py, propose.py, surface.py), takeoff/README.md and RUNBOOK.md, existing spikes kept as seeds. SharePoint: Takeoff Ledger library (ledger.csv, corrections.jsonl, calibration.csv, egress.csv, project register), per-project folders (primitives.json, sheet.json, bq.json, rules/<contract>.json, quantity sheets, claim packs), regression corpus of real sheets, Bluebeam tool chest. Office PC: nightly scheduled tasks for harvest, import, shadow, propose and surface jobs.

roadmap.goal: Establish the baseline and the safety definitions, seed the item library and two rulebooks, ship engine.js and capture app v1, and run TRENCH/CHAMBER in shadow on live tenders with no drawing AI.
deliverables: Inbox sample and tool census; project register with tiers; money-bearing error, accuracy definition and per-class tolerances signed
Timer page; two-QS blind baseline on ~20 sheets
items.json v0 from 3-5 live Price Documents with a count of BQ lines by family
engine.js TRENCH and CHAMBER with goldens and CI; rulebooks for 2 live contracts 100% confirmed
Capture app v1 with per-viewport scale grader, typed tables, xlsx out; 3 live tenders in shadow (QS commits first)
Harvester go/no-go at week 8; claims.html v1 in shadow on 2 contracts by week 13
gates: >=200 derived lines across >=3 tenders with every engine-vs-QS difference root-caused (QS slip, rule gap or engine bug -> golden test)
Inter-QS disagreement per class tabulated and adopted as the accuracy ceiling
Month-3 stop-loss: TRENCH/CHAMBER to Stage 2 only if zero unexplained differences; DR coverage on the 2 claim pilots reported

gates: Timer shows derived-family minutes per sheet down >=30% vs baseline on A/B sheets
Zero money-bearing errors in engine lines; rulebook coverage 100% confirmed for each family in Stage 2
Claim pack within 2% of the QS pack for 2 consecutive months on >=3 pilot contracts; DR Verify coverage >=90% of claim-relevant rows on pilots

assumptions: Hour shares are the digest's low-confidence inference (tender 40%, claims and subcon certification 27%, VOs 12%, ordering and final account 12%, other 9%) until the week-2 time log replaces them; every figure below is re-derived from the measured shares at month 3.

Within tender hours, arithmetic and bookkeeping (CIS RC build-ups ~15%, trench runs and derived lines ~15-20%, BQ entry and reconciliation ~15-20%) are ~50%; the Stage 2 saving on that block is taken as 30% at month 6 (not the Rulebook's 40%, per the MD judge's point that QS Excel templates already do some arithmetic), 50% at month 12 (Stage 3) and 60% at month 24.

Claims: assist on 5 of ~30 contracts at 30% faster by month 6 (1.4 points); auto-draft on 15 contracts at 50% faster by month 12 (6.8 points); all ~30 at 60% faster by month 24 (16 points); each conditional on DR coverage >=90% on the contract.

Measured primitives contribute nothing before month 13; by month 24 counts and lengths at Stage 2/3 on vector PDF and DXF cut the measuring share of tender hours (~20%) by 40% and the section tool cuts the bulk-from-levels share (~17%) by 20%, together ~5 points.
VO differential 35% faster on 12% share (4 points) and ordering/final account 30% faster on 12% share (3.6 points) by month 24.

Verification overhead, rulebook confirmation, blind-then-reveal, seeded errors, audits and one manual sheet per QS per week cost +1 point at month 6 and about 3 points at steady state; 15-20% of items stay human-touched in every graduated class.

Month 6 = 100 - 6 (tender arithmetic) - 1.4 (claims) + 1 (overhead) ~ 93; month 12 = 100 - 10 - 6.8 - 1.8 (ordering) + 1 ~ 82; month 24 = 100 - 12 - 5 - 16 - 4 - 3.6 + 3 ~ 62-65, quoted as 65 with 55-60 as the upside if claims reach Stage 4 on most contracts and lengths graduate on >=3 originator templates; 68-72 if auto-lengths stay in Stage 1 or DR coverage lags.
Builder at 0.4 FTE (21 pw/yr); at 0.3 FTE the 24-month figure becomes the 30-month figure.
effort_curve.how_measured: Wall-clock minutes per sheet per class from the in-app start/pause timer (self-report and annotation timestamps are not accepted), aggregated weekly as minutes per sheet by class and source, QS-touch rate, automation rate and audited accuracy (reported separately, medical-coding vocabulary), escaped-error rate, time-to-first-quantity on a new tender, claim-pack minutes per contract, and QS minutes per S$1m of measured quantity. Reduction is proven by alternating-sheet A/B assignment inside the same tender and alternating-month A/B on the same contract for claims, so learning-curve effects cannot masquerade as gains. The denominator is KKL's own two-week time log per QS, not the digest's shares. Effort figures are published on the ledger dashboard against the Stage 0 baseline; the month-3, month-6 and month-12 stop-loss reviews read only these numbers.

costs.one_off_and_services: Run cost breakdown (planning figure US$250/month): Claude API text-only about US$100-150/month (about 5 tenders/month x preamble, BQ-line and schedule extraction plus ticket/DO extraction on KKL's own documents, Sonnet-class lane, Batch API overnight); provision of about US$100/month covering either an Artifex commercial licence for PyMuPDF if legal rejects the internal-use AGPL position (US$1-2k/yr, assumption) or Bluebeam Core seats for QSs who annotate but lack Core (US$330/user/yr; 4-6 seats = US$110-165/month; zero if not needed or already licensed). Already paid: GitHub Pages, SharePoint/M365, one office PC. One-off: civils.ai Starter benchmark trial 3 months x US$90 = US$270 on Tier C sheets only; optional Kreo not bought. Per-project, charged to the contract and excluded from the monthly figure: vendor RTK drone survey S$2.5-10k per visit (only where a bulk open-cut site, the bq_map paid_on basis and airspace/IPA status justify it), CAAS permits handled by the vendor. Not in scope: GPU, Azure VM, Gemini/Vertex lane, YOLO training, FastAPI runner (all rejected). Builder capacity: 41.5 pw over 24 months equals 0.4 FTE with no slack; at 0.3 FTE year-2 items slip about six months; at 0.5 FTE the slack goes to the scan route and capture app v2 earlier.
costs.qs_time_cost: Chief QS: about 1 day/week for months 0-3 (item library, two rulebooks, root-causing shadow differences, baseline), then about 0.5 day/week (rulebook confirmation per tender under 1 hour, weekly triage of reason-coded disagreements sorted by value, monthly audits) = roughly 11 person-weeks over 24 months. Two QSs: the blind baseline on ~20 sheets (about 2 days each). All QSs: about 2 hours/week each in year 1 for corrections, blind-then-reveal sheets and seeded-error review, plus one fully manual sheet per week from month 6 (skill maintenance), which the timer counts as overhead in the effort curve. Contracts person: about 2 person-weeks over 24 months (tiers, NDA and OSA readings, preamble and paid_on confirmations, insurer note, stop-loss reviews). MD: three stop-loss reviews of about half a day each. Site QSs: 1 day per claim pilot contract to align DR coverage. The Shadow Ledger's '1 hour/week' chief QS figure is not used; disagreement volume on real sheets is triaged by reason code and value so that only money-bearing disagreements are adjudicated.

build_vs_buy: Build the spine, buy only what no in-house code can replace, and measure a vendor against KKL's own sheets rather than argue about it. No surveyed product covers KKL's actual work: civils.ai (Singapore company, US servers, Starter US$90 and Professional US$270 per user per month, US$9 per takeoff with engineer QA in 24 hours, one takeoff = one trade on one sheet up to 1:250, cut/fill 'coming soon', '97%' self-reported, API/MCP and DPA only on Enterprise) cannot receive Tier A drawings under the OSA, LTA NDAs or the Infrastructure Protection Act, exposes no geometry or per-class accuracy, and knows nothing of per-contract preambles, DR Capture, monthly SOPA claims or subcon certification, which is where most of the recurring hours sit; Kreo (US$35-175/month) has building classes only, is cloud-only and returns measurements via API only on Pro by request or Enterprise; Togal exports Excel only with no API; STACK and PlanSwift return quantities, not vertices. Bluebeam is a capture source, not a takeoff engine: seats are bought only if the week-1 sample shows QSs annotate and lack Core. What KKL buys: Claude API usage for text-only reading on cleared tiers (already in the workbench); a three-month civils.ai Starter trial on Tier C sheets (public LTA SDRE sheets and KKL's own past tenders) purely as an external benchmark of the in-house engine's counts, lengths and areas, with results written into the ledger; vendor RTK flights per project; possibly a PyMuPDF commercial licence. Quarterly re-check owned by the builder and contracts person: does civils.ai or Kreo now offer civil classes, Singapore hosting, per-class audited accuracy or an API that returns geometry; if all four appear, the item library, rulebooks, bq_map, ledger and claims module remain KKL's and only the measurer underneath would be swapped. The 'buy civils.ai during a builder gap' fallback applies to Tier C sheets only and never to claims. Written conclusion for the MD: the in-house route is the only route for Tier A contracts and for claims regardless of price; for Tier C tender sheets it costs about 15.5 builder person-weeks (auto-primitives) against US$9 per sheet-trade, which the benchmark trial will price in KKL's own error terms before phase-2 budget is released.
governance_summary: The staged framework is applied per item class x drawing source with two kinds of gate: deterministic derived families (TRENCH, CHAMBER, RC-SECTION, PAVEMENT, KERB) graduate on 100% page-cited, QS-confirmed rulebook parameters plus golden tests plus 300 root-caused clean lines, while measured primitives graduate on the digest's statistical gates (>=200 items, >=5 projects, >=2 sources, median <=1% vector or <=3% scan, p95 <=5%, counts >=98% exact, zero confident-wrong, then >=500 verified items, accept-without-edit >=95%, escaped-error <=0.5%, no money-bearing error in the last 300, auto-accept bucket empirical error <=0.5% by check pattern). Money-bearing error is defined in writing before Stage 1 (larger of 2% of item value or S$2,000 for claims and subcon lines, S$10,000 for a tender line). Rollback is automatic: any money-bearing error in an auto-accepted stream returns the class to Stage 2 until 300 clean items; audit error rate above 2x baseline raises the audit rate to 10%; any new originator template or source routes to review until 50 clean items; any engine, rulebook, library or code change re-runs the full regression corpus and returns the class to shadow for 100 items on any regression; monthly drift review acts only when a distribution shift coincides with an audit accuracy drop. Automation-bias and deskilling controls: blind-then-reveal on a 20% sample, seeded known-error items with catch rate >=90% per QS, one fully manual sheet per QS per week, juniors six months with reveal disabled, quarterly blind re-baseline within 5% of Stage 0 skill, reviewers scored on catch rate not throughput, time saved banked as tender capacity in year one. Roles: chief QS and builder jointly own the engine's mistakes through an incident log where every escaped error gets a root cause and a regression test; the contracts person owns tiers, NDA/OSA readings, paid_on confirmations and the insurer notification; a named QS signs every bid, claim, VO and subcon certificate and the engine never signs; PSSCOC Module A and SOP Act exposure stays with the named signatory. Budget control: stop-loss reviews at month 3 (derived-family minutes down >=30% on pilot tenders; DR coverage >=90% on claim pilots), month 6 (claim packs within 2% for two months; zero money-bearing errors in engine lines) and month 12 (corpus results) release each subsequent budget tranche, including the 8.5 pw auto-primitive phase 2. Builder risk: single-file apps plus one Python job package, pure functions with golden tests, rulebooks and item library as QS-owned data, README and runbook per milestone, a named second maintainer by month 6, confidential regression sheets on SharePoint only.

key_claims.claim: At least 50% of BQ lines by count (and 40% by value) on KKL's live LTA/HDB/PUB Price Documents are deterministic functions of four primitives plus the rulebook and SDRE lookups (digest inference ~60%).

key_claims.claim: Each contract's measurement preambles reduce to about 40 machine-checkable parameters without free-text exceptions the engine cannot apply.

key_claims.if_false: Add an exception-clause field per family that routes the affected family to Stage 2 on that contract permanently; families graduate per contract, never globally; chief QS confirmation time rises.

key_claims.claim: A QS can type or trace the primitives for a family in no more than 40% of the time now spent producing the family's lines by hand, i.e. their existing Excel templates do not already absorb most of the arithmetic (MD judge's objection to the Rulebook's 30-40%).
key_claims.why_it_matters: This is the whole month-6 tender saving; verification work must be less than measuring removed.
key_claims.how_to_test: Stage 0 timer plus alternating-sheet A/B inside the same tender in months 3-6 on >=10 sheets per QS.
key_claims.if_false: Stage 2 sheets at >=80% of baseline minutes means the saving is only BQ entry and reconciliation (~15-20% of tender hours); month-12 becomes ~88-90; effort shifts to the harvester (zero-entry primitives) and claims, and typed tables are dropped for direct workbook import.

key_claims.claim: At least half of the sheets QSs measure carry PDF measurement annotations readable by PyMuPDF (Shadow Ledger's premise; unverified, and real Revu keys were tested only on a synthetic file).
key_claims.why_it_matters: Decides whether the zero-behaviour-change harvester exists, whether Bluebeam seats are bought, and where Stage 2 review happens.
key_claims.how_to_test: Week-1 inbox and folder sample; extract_markups.py on one real KKL Revu file checking /VP, /BSIColumnData and Count.

key_claims.claim: DR Capture/DR Verify rows on the claim pilot contracts carry activity_code, struct/method/spec_element, chainage or zone and depth_band on >=90% of claim-relevant rows (unverified per all three judges).

key_claims.if_false: Claims stay in shadow on that contract; validation rules are pushed into DR Capture and site coaching follows the coverage report; the claims contribution slips six months and month-12 is ~88.

key_claims.claim: Inter-QS disagreement per class today is at least as large as the engine's post-gate error (>=1% on lengths, >=3% on areas), so the digest's gates are passable, and engine-vs-QS disagreement on derived lines after rule reconciliation is smaller than inter-QS disagreement.

key_claims.how_to_test: Two-QS blind baseline on ~20 sheets in weeks 2-4; shadow ledger versus that baseline from week 6.
key_claims.if_false: Set each class's gate to the measured ceiling; classes where the ceiling is tighter than the engine can reach stay in assist; derived families whose disagreement exceeds the ceiling are root-caused before any Stage 2.

key_claims.if_false: Below 50%: phase 2 (8.5 pw) is cut to DXF, counts and tracing; the scan route budget rises; month-24 stays ~72-75 with the spine and claims carrying the saving.

key_claims.claim: On real layerless, all-black sheets, pen weight, dash, closure, parallel-partner offset, hatch class, symbol signature and label regex reach >=80% per-path precision on measurable classes after no more than 20 corrected sheets from one originator template (TrueLine's >=90% lowered per the judges; no civil dataset exists to pre-train on).

The builder's confirmed FTE allocation, who the second maintainer is, and whether legal requires an Artifex commercial licence for internal PyMuPDF use.
Confirmation that the office PC can run nightly scheduled tasks over OneDrive-synced folders without sync conflicts, and which SharePoint library will hold the ledger and regression corpus.

rejected.idea: FastAPI local runner with Entra ID sign-in, DuckDB ledger and an Azure VM
rejected.why_rejected_or_deferred: A server outside the single-file plus CSV house style that one part-time builder cannot maintain; every job runs as a nightly Python task on the office PC and every app is a static page.

rejected.idea: Four-model VLM benchmark harness (Gemini 3 Pro via Vertex, Claude, GPT-5.x, local Qwen2.5-VL) and a Gemini lane for dense drawing reads
rejected.why_rejected_or_deferred: Fragments the Claude workbench KKL already has, adds scope to an over-committed builder, and drawing pixels cannot leave KKL on Tier A anyway; the only benchmark bought is civils.ai Starter on Tier C sheets.

rejected.idea: VLM schedule reads (sizes, IL/GL, BBS totals) promoted to Stage 3 by month 6 on a claimed 98% cell accuracy
rejected.why_rejected_or_deferred: These are money-bearing attributes and the digest's structured-extraction evidence is 25-37% recall with up to 56% hallucination zero-shot; Extract stays in Stage 2 with mandatory citations, column-sum reconciliation and plan-count cross-checks, Stage 3 only after >=500 verified rows.

rejected.idea: T1 tier sending drawing crops to cloud models for client tender documents without NDA/OSA marking
rejected.why_rejected_or_deferred: The Official Secrets Act covers drawings regardless of marking and LTA tenders are NDA-gated; the default is Tier A and only text may leave on cleared projects.

rejected.idea: YOLOv8/ultralytics symbol detector exported to ONNX and run with onnxruntime-web, with GPU training
rejected.why_rejected_or_deferred: Deferred beyond month 24: no civil dataset exists, it needs >=2,000 logged instances per symbol family and a licence-clean detector, and counts on vector sheets come exactly from geometry.

rejected.idea: Every module implemented twice (import_pdf.py and import-pdfjs.js, scale.py and scale.js, kernel.py and kernel.js, calc in both) with shared test vectors, plus a HistGradientBoosting class map exported to a hand-rolled JSON tree for the browser
rejected.why_rejected_or_deferred: A one-person maintenance trap in which every fix lands twice; the measurer is built once in Python as a nightly shadow job, pdf.js is used only for on-screen snapping, dual-route agreement is a periodic corpus test, and an ML class map is trained only if rules plateau and evaluated only in Python.

rejected.idea: TrueLine's 42 person-week total with 30 in year one at 0.4 FTE, and the Rulebook's ~10 builder-days for vector-PDF auto-measure
rejected.why_rejected_or_deferred: Both arithmetic claims fail per the judges: 0.4 FTE is 21 pw a year, and ten days cannot buy viewports, scale, classification and a kernel on real sheets; the merged plan holds year one to 20.5 pw and gives auto-primitives 15.5 pw across phases 2-4.

rejected.idea: Fortnightly vendor RTK drone flights as a platform cost (S$9,000/month, US$7,500/month run cost) and survey-first sequencing with tender deferred to month 9
rejected.why_rejected_or_deferred: The economics do not close against a first-year saving the design itself put at ~5%, the critical path runs through CAAS permits, IPA status of MRT sites and MC acceptance of a shared surface, and the brief asks for drawing takeoff; the surface engine survives as a per-project module with flights charged to the contract.

rejected.idea: Annotation timestamps (/M, /CreationDate) as the per-sheet per-class effort baseline
rejected.why_rejected_or_deferred: Revu may write dates at save and a markup span conflates thinking, site calls and lunch with measuring; the start/pause timer is the only accepted effort evidence.

rejected.idea: Chief QS adjudication of shadow disagreements in 1 hour per week
rejected.why_rejected_or_deferred: Real layerless sheets will produce hundreds of engine-noise disagreements in the first months; the plan budgets 1 day/week for three months then 0.5 day/week, triages by reason code and value, and adjudicates only money-bearing disagreements so un-adjudicated noise never enters truth.

rejected.idea: Loads x truck capacity / bulking as a claim quantity
rejected.from_design: Surface Ledger (as cross-check) and DR practice
rejected.why_rejected_or_deferred: Truck-count volumes are systematically unreliable; loads are a KPI and calibration source for m3/load, bulking and m3/h feeding tender rates, never the claim source unless the preamble pays per load.

rejected.idea: Kreo Pro as a second-opinion measurement API; Bluebeam Max for AI/MCP features; ODA File Converter
rejected.why_rejected_or_deferred: Kreo has no civil classes and is cloud-only; Bluebeam Max features are irrelevant to capture; ODA's terms are non-commercial for non-members, so LibreDWG dwg2dxf runs as a separate process instead.

rejected.idea: Contour-to-DEM reconstruction from PDF or scanned contour sheets, and IFC/CORENET X tooling
rejected.why_rejected_or_deferred: Scan-to-DEM is research-grade with no turnkey pipeline; IFC-SG is a building-permit regime that does not reach civil earthworks in 2026-27; volumes come from surfaces or QS-picked sections, and IFC is handled ad hoc if it ever arrives.

rejected.idea: A global rulebook or client-wide rule defaults applied without per-contract confirmation
rejected.why_rejected_or_deferred: Preambles are contract-specific under PSSCOC Module A; client templates seed a draft but every money-bearing parameter is confirmed per contract against its cited page or the family is blocked.

rejected.idea: Counting labels as the product or promising the 24-month figure as 55%
rejected.from_design: Overlay (confirmations as labels), Rulebook and Shadow Ledger (55% curves)
rejected.why_rejected_or_deferred: Labels are a by-product; only timer minutes count. The 55% figure is quoted as the upside, not the plan, because it needs both the claims roll-up at Stage 4 on most contracts and auto-lengths graduating, neither evidenced yet.
